editorial: Today, in the developer ecosystem, embodied agents that interact with the physical world and audit frameworks targeting the security vulnerabilities of large language models (LLMs) are coming to the fore. New tools on GitHub and Hugging Face focus on both the management of hardware-based systems and privacy testing for distributed models.

items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.summary: The security-audit-skill developed by Cloudflare is a JavaScript-based capability package that turns software agents into auditors capable of performing multi-stage security audits. This tool manages processes ranging from discovery to reporting with independently verifiable and machine-readable findings.

snapshot.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings. A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

items.title: NVIDIA/OpenShell
items.summary: OpenShell, developed by NVIDIA, offers a secure and privacy-focused runtime environment for autonomous AI agents. Written in Rust, this tool audits data access by limiting the capabilities of agents, such as reading files or using APIs (a digital bridge that allows two different software programs to talk to each other), within the framework of specific policies.

snapshot.description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents. OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.

items.title: aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws
items.summary: The aws/agent-toolkit-for-aws offered by Amazon Web Services includes official tools, plugins, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that enable AI agents to develop, deploy, and manage applications on AWS. This Python-based toolkit allows AI agents to work more compatibly with AWS infrastructure in software development processes.

snapshot.description: Official, AWS-supported MCP servers, skills, and plugins to help AI agents build on AWS. Help AI coding agents build, deploy, and manage applications on AWS.

items.title: Nutlope/hallmark
items.summary: Nutlope/hallmark offers a design skill that prevents content created on AI-powered code editors like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex from looking like it was generated by AI. This tool aims to visually individualize standard AI outputs that emerge during software development processes.

snapshot.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.

items.title: luongnv89/claude-howto
items.summary: luongnv89/claude-howto provides a visual and example-oriented guide for Claude Code, ranging from basic concepts to advanced agent structures. It aims to facilitate AI-powered coding processes with copy-paste templates that users can apply directly.

snapshot.description: A visual, example-driven guide to Claude Code — from basic concepts to advanced agents, with copy-paste templates that bring immediate value.

items.title: pbakaus/impeccable
items.summary: pbakaus/impeccable offers a design language and guidance system that AI coding agents can use when designing interfaces. Developed in Rust, this tool aims to improve frontend designs generated by AI through 24 commands and 62 deterministic detector rules.

snapshot.description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design. Design guidance for AI coding agents. 1 skill, 24 commands, live browser iteration, and 62 deterministic detector rules for AI-generated frontend design.

items.title: pollen-robotics/microduck
items.summary: microduck, developed by Pollen Robotics, is a 25-centimeter bipedal duck robot project powered by a Rockchip RK3566 processor. The software, written in Rust, manages fifteen servos via neural policies to execute the robot's movement and control processes.

snapshot.description: A Tiny biped duck robot 🦆. This repo is the duck's brain. About 25 cm and 800 g of robot, run by a handful of daemons on a Rockchip RK3566: a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies, the radios and the camera, and the update machinery that gets new software onto a robot without bricking it.

items.title: google-gemini/gemini-cli
items.summary: gemini-cli, developed by Google, is an open-source (source code accessible to everyone) tool that provides direct access to the Gemini AI model via the terminal. The software allows users to create AI prompts quickly and lightweight in a command-line environment.

snapshot.description: An open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal. Gemini CLI is an open-source AI agent that brings the power of Gemini directly into your terminal. It provides lightweight access to Gemini, giving you the most direct path from your prompt to our model.

items.title: makecindy/cindy
items.summary: Cindy is an open-source (source code open for access and development) AI agent designed to complete real work in your projects and applications, working right out of the box. It combines multiple models and tools into a single structure, allowing users to manage their workflows.

snapshot.description: Consider it done. The open-source AI agent that works out of the box · 想到，就能做到。开源、开箱即用的 AI Agent。. Cindy is an open-source AI agent that works out of the box. She brings multiple harnesses, models and tools into one agent that finishes real work in your projects and apps. Ready from day one, yours to shape over time.

items.title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you
items.summary: Local Wikipedia is an encyclopedia project that provides information about places within a half-hour walking distance of the user's current location. It serves as a locally customized version of the online information source Wikipedia.

snapshot.description: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you.

items.title: Show HN: Steal My Bitcoin
items.summary: Steal My Bitcoin is a platform created to test how a recently discovered PHP remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability can be exploited in the real world. The developer invites users to access the system to observe the concrete effects of this security vulnerability.

snapshot.description: Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE we spent the last few days panicking over. Have fun!

items.title: The Goose Programming Language
items.summary: The Goose is a new programming language designed for low-level system programming languages. It aims to develop system software with a structure focused on memory safety and performance.

snapshot.description: https://twitter.com/ID_AA_Carmack/status/2113704269274636568

items.title: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell, blast radius affects many HTTP libs and apps
items.summary: The evolution of the Node2Shell vulnerability into HTTP2Shell puts numerous HTTP libraries and applications that use the Brotli data compression algorithm at risk. To avoid being affected by this vulnerability, coded as CVE-2026-111497, it is necessary to check the versions used and perform updates.

snapshot.description: The Brotli flaw behind Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) affects many libraries and applications using HTTP with Brotli or brotlicffi installed. Check your versions and upgrade to the fix.

items.title: I don't understand quantum physics (2018)
items.summary: This resource, prepared by the University of Southampton, covers the fundamental concepts of quantum physics and the difficult-to-understand points in this field. Focusing on the complexity of physical phenomena, the study explains the principles of quantum physics within an academic framework.

items.title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is an updated version of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model, an artificial intelligence model capable of processing visual and textual data. It aims to provide cost efficiency by reducing processing time and output length while increasing its performance in reasoning, coding, and agent-based tasks.

snapshot.description: image-text-to-text model. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.

items.title: RecursiveSI/flint
items.summary: Flint, developed by RecursiveSI, is a mixture-of-experts text generation model designed for coding agents. With a total of 39.8 billion parameters, the model was developed for the purposes of examining codebases, debugging, adding features, and writing tests.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. Flint is Recursive’s mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents, with 39.8 billion total parameters and approximately 2.5 billion active per token. It is designed to investigate codebases, fix bugs, implement features, and write tests.

items.title: black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy
items.summary: flux-3-image-klein-comfy, developed by Black Forest Labs, is an artificial intelligence model that provides image-to-image conversion. The model is designed to work in harmony with visual-based workflow tools such as ComfyUI.

snapshot.description: image-to-image model

items.title: XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B
items.summary: Spark-X2.6-4B, published on the Hugging Face platform, is an artificial intelligence model focused on text generation. Using the same architecture as its previous version, the model offers performance improvements in areas such as coding, reasoning, and multilingual content processing thanks to post-training improvements.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. Spark-X2.6-4B retains exactly the same architecture as Spark-X2.5-4B, achieving its capability gains through improved post-training. It delivers substantial improvements in coding, agent, long-context, multilingual, reasoning, etc. These advances enable more capable and practical on-device AI for developers and users tackling real-world tasks.

items.title: Lightricks/LTX-2.5
items.summary: LTX-2.5, developed by Lightricks, is an image-to-video model that converts images into moving videos. Shared on the Hugging Face platform, this model allows visual content to be animated via artificial intelligence.

snapshot.description: image-to-video model

items.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
items.summary: TARSphere is a robot-focused full-stack framework developed for long-term embodied agents moving under physical and social constraints. The TARSphere-Infra component offers the opportunity to test robot policies in physics simulators with constrained dialogues and embodied artificial intelligence characters (NPCs).

snapshot.description: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue.

items.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
items.summary: LLM-Attacker, shared by Hugging Face, is a framework developed to evaluate privacy vulnerabilities in fragmented and distributed large language models (LLMs). This system helps researchers compare attack methods and standardize security analyses for data reconstruction.

snapshot.description: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictio

items.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
items.summary: EvalResearchBench is a research benchmark that examines whether artificial intelligence agents can automatically generate the evaluation feedback they need in recursive self-improvement processes. This study presents a method that aims for agents to design their own evaluations in order to reduce the cost of complex testing processes.

snapshot.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research. items.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
items.summary: Diffusion language models have the ability to generate multiple tokens in a single forward pass and decide how many passes to perform during generation. Analyses show that the cost of these models varies depending on the task type, operating faster for simple operations where input text is copied, and slower for tasks requiring free writing.

snapshot.description: Diffusion language models can write several tokens in one forward pass, and they decide during generation how many passes to spend. Two outputs of the same token length can therefore vary a lot in cost. To understand the underlying factors of this cost variation, we analyze two diffusion models across 10 tasks. items.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: T 2Quant, developed for Diffusion Language Models (DLMs), optimizes this process by determining that quantization precision varies according to tasks and time steps. The method offers a mixed-precision structure by estimating the precision levels required for different tasks without needing any labels or metrics.

snapshot.description: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) introduce unique quantization challenges due to their iterative denoising process. In this work, we reveal that quantization sensitivity is both taskand time-dependent, with different downstream tasks exhibiting distinct precision requirements across denoising steps. We further show that these patterns can be predicted without groundtruth labels or task-specific evaluation metrics. glossary.explanation: The fundamental environment required for software to run, operating in the background.
A connection protocol that enables artificial intelligence models to communicate with different data sources and tools in a standardized way.
A visual editing capability that makes AI-generated content appear more natural and human-made.
A control mechanism that allows software to detect errors or specific features through a precise and immutable set of rules.
The side of a website or application that is seen and interacted with by the user.
Decision-making rules determined by artificial neural networks to control a robot's movements.
An interface that allows providing text-based instructions to a computer via a command line.
A serious security vulnerability that allows an attacker to remotely control software on another computer and execute their own code.
The branch of physics that studies the behavior and energy levels of subatomic particles.
An artificial intelligence architecture where small sub-models, each specialized in different subjects, are used together to solve complex tasks.
An artificial intelligence process that transforms an image into a different style or content based on it.
The ability to generate meaningful and coherent texts according to given prompts.
Artificial intelligence technology that converts a static image into an animated video clip.
Robotic artificial intelligence systems that can move in the physical world, perceive their environment, and react accordingly.
A holistic structure that encompasses both the visible front-end and all background infrastructure processes of a software.
Characters in games or simulations that are not controlled by the player and move with artificial intelligence.
